takeaway: Calot's triangle is bordered by the inferior border of the liver, the cystic duct and the common hepatic duct. The cystic artery, from the right hepatic artery, lies within it.

lines.text: A woman has a cholecystectomy, weeks after an episode of acute cholecystitis.
To find the cystic artery, the surgeon first identifies Calot's triangle.
lines.say: (clears throat) To find the cystic artery, the surgeon first identifies Calot's triangle.

lines.text: Its upper border is the inferior border of the liver.
One side is the cystic duct,
and the other is the common hepatic duct.
So the answer: the common hepatic duct, the inferior border of the liver, and the cystic duct.
The cystic artery, a branch of the right hepatic artery, lies inside this triangle.
Biliary anatomy varies a lot, so identify these structures before any dissection.
